input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "preservation",
 "diagnosis": "The loop invariants only bound low from below and relate it to high (0 <= low <= high + 1); nothing bounds high above by arr.Length - 1. Inside the loop, Dafny assumes only the invariants and the guard, so it cannot show mid = (low + high) / 2 < arr.Length, and arr[mid] at line 17 is flagged as index out of range (counterexample: arr.Length = 12930, high = 12929 is fine in reality but the invariant does not exclude larger high). The invariant needs the upper bound high < arr.Length, which holds initially (high = arr.Length - 1) and is maintained (high only decreases). The 'not target' invariant is also strengthened to the standard form (indices below low or above high do not hold target) so that it is preserved using sortedness and implies not_found at exit."}
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='program.dfy'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""        invariant 0 <= low <= high + 1
        invariant forall i :: 0 <= i <= low && high <= i < arr.Length ==> arr[i] != target""","""        invariant 0 <= low <= high + 1 <= arr.Length
        invariant forall i :: 0 <= i < arr.Length && (i < low || high < i) ==> arr[i] != target""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
program.dfy now verifies: 6 verified, 0 errors.

**What was wrong:** The loop invariant didn't put an upper limit on `high`. It only said `0 <= low <= high + 1`. Inside the loop, Dafny knows only the invariants and the loop condition, so it couldn't prove `mid = (low + high) / 2 < arr.Length`. That made `arr[mid]` at line 17 a possible out-of-range access. I wrote this up in `diagnosis.json` as an invariant / preservation failure.

**The fix** (loop invariants at lines 13–14):
```dafny
invariant 0 <= low <= high + 1 <= arr.Length
invariant forall i :: 0 <= i < arr.Length && (i < low || high < i) ==> arr[i] != target
```
- **First line:** adds the missing limit `high < arr.Length`. It holds at the start because `high` begins at `arr.Length - 1`, and it stays true because `high` only goes down.
- **Second line:** I also replaced the old "target is not here" invariant. It said `0 <= i <= low && high <= i`, which is only true when `low == high`, so it didn't describe what binary search actually rules out. The new version says target is not at any index below `low` or above `high`. Sortedness keeps it true from one iteration to the next. When the loop ends (`low > high`), it covers every index, which gives `not_found`.

I also removed a deprecated semicolon at line 57 because it caused a warning.

**One problem I didn't change:** the `distinct` predicate is wrong. Its quantifier includes the case `i == j`, which demands `arr[i] != arr[i]`. That is only possible for an empty array, so `requires distinct(arr)` effectively restricts the method to empty arrays. The method still verifies, but anyone calling it with a non-empty array couldn't meet this precondition. The intended version is probably `forall i, j :: 0 <= i < j < arr.Length ==> arr[i] != arr[j]`. I left it alone because the task was the index error. The new invariants rely only on `sorted`, so fixing `distinct` shouldn't affect this proof, but I haven't run the verifier with that change.
